analyst_view.overall: Early view: the two promoted sides meet. Paderborn are described as physical and high-pressing and drew 2-2 with Frankfurt last time out; Elversberg under Vincent Wagner have been the league's entertainers, with 4-3 wins over Augsburg and at Gladbach and a spirited 2-1 loss at Dortmund. Both have a few knocks (Marcel Hoffmeier for Paderborn, Jan Gyamerah and Lukas Pinckert for Elversberg) that should mostly clear by December.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean higher: Elversberg's games have been open, with two seven-goal matches already, and they keep attacking even when behind, as they did at Dortmund. Paderborn's pressing also tends to make games stretched.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.2 corners. Both sides play forward and Elversberg scored from a short corner routine at Dortmund. The site's figure already looks fair.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards. Paderborn's pressing is physical, but neither side has a bad discipline record in what I read, and the referee is not known. I see no reason to move it yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.5 shots. Two attacking promoted teams should produce plenty of attempts, which the model already expects, so I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Given how many goals Elversberg's games have produced, with Maurice Krattenmacher and Noel Futkeu both scoring, I lean a little higher on attempts that test the goalkeeper.
